claim: For independent integer-valued \(X_1,X_2,X_3\) with each maximal point mass at most \(\alpha\), where \(1/3\le\alpha\le1/2\), the exact sharp supremum of \(\Pr(X_1+X_2+X_3=s)\) over integer \(s\) and all such laws equals \(7\alpha^3-6\alpha^2+2\alpha\) for \(\alpha\le2/5\), and \(3\alpha^2(1-\alpha)\) for \(\alpha\ge2/5\). The two phases have explicit three-point extremizers, and the value at \(\alpha=2/5\) agrees.

correctness.rationale: A greedy extreme-point reduction reduces each count law to weights (alpha,alpha,1-2alpha). Elementary two-set representation counting yields 3,4,5,7 as the sharp universal triples upper bounds. Unless all three full supports have seven representations, the normalized atom bound is 3+3t; the equality-seven case rigidly forces aligned three-term progressions and then has exactly six polynomial profiles, maximized by 3+2t+2t^2. The maximum of these two branches crosses at t=1/2 (alpha=2/5); explicit mixed and matching laws attain both branches. An exact-rational verifier checks all 27 profiles and six parameter witnesses; the proof itself covers infinite integer supports.

value.rationale: The finite n=3, inverse-atom-cap between 2 and 3 slice is a naturally motivated unresolved point of the recent finite exact concentration conjecture. Its exact sharp bound is not a textbook consequence of the even-summand theorem and exhibits a genuine change in the configuration of the extremal three-atom laws at alpha=2/5. Both a universal inequality and explicit attainability are provided.
